text:
alex: heads up — CI red on //runtime:handshake_unit_test in the nightly matrix (linux/arm64). intermittent failure, not blocked on a single test run but >1 in last 10.

sam: link? buildkite job id?

alex: https://buildkite.com/redwood/runtime/builds/7890#job-5 — failure is assertion in handshake::complete(): expected session_order == 1 but got 0. no obvious stacktrace noise.

buildkite-bot: Job failed: test //runtime:handshake_unit_test (attempt #3) — see logs above.

maria: hmm. last green was 3973950000, PRs since then touched timer ordering and session startup path. alex which PRs are suspect?

alex: PR #4219 touched timer jitter logic but only in prefetched path. PR #4227 adjusted handshake retry backoff. both small.

sam: can we rerun the single test 50x on CI to get failure rate? if it's nondet we should bisect.

alex: scheduling a rerun now with runs_per_test=50.

ci-bot: Rerun started: //runtime:handshake_unit_test — 50 runs flagged. will post summary when done.

jin: while that runs, can someone try local stress with a seed sweep? i can try `bazel test //runtime:handshake_unit_test --runs_per_test=100 --test_arg=--seed=0..99` on my M1. may highlight arch-specific timing.

alex: thanks. also capture `RUST_LOG=debug` if you can. the failing line only shows ordering mismatch, might be a race in backoff timer wake.

maria: if rerun reproduces, let's bisect between 3973950000..3974002000 (includes both PRs). if it's flaky only under high concurrency we might need a repro harness.

sam: quick diff check: PR #4227 changed retry window from 10ms jitter to 5-15ms. small but could flip ordering under arm cache.

jin: running local now. will paste a short log if it fails.

alex: thx. if anyone has cycles, try running under `--nocapture --test-threads=1` to see if serializing tests hides it. I suspect it's a real inter-thread ordering issue, not test harness flakiness.

ci-bot: Rerun summary: 50 runs — 2 failures (4%). Failures consistent with session_order mismatch. Attached logs: https://buildkite.com/redwood/runtime/builds/7890/artifacts/handshake-flake-summary.txt

maria: 4% is high enough. starting bisect with git bisect run + automated test script. assigning to alex/sam to watch.

alex: ack — starting bisect job now. will report the first bad commit.

sam: pinging @eng-runtime on the PRs that touched timers in case others have context. :eyes:

jin: local run hit the same assertion after ~120 iterations. attaching snippet:```
thread 'test_handshake' panicked at 'assertion failed: session_order == 1 (got 0)', src/handshake/mod.rs:248
stack backtrace:
 0: handshake::complete::{{closure}}
 1: runtime::timer::wake
 2: std::thread::{{impl}}::spawn::{{closure}}
```

maria: good repro — suggests scheduling/timer wake interplay. once bisect yields a commit we can add a small deterministic test or tighten the backoff ordering.

alex: bisect found first bad commit: 3973971112 — PR #4227 (retry backoff change). reverting locally makes the test pass with 0/500 failures.

sam: great find. proposed fix: restore old jitter window and add a regression test that exercises two concurrent handshake attempts with controlled clocks.

maria: yep. please open a PR that reverts the change and includes the test + comment explaining the flake. also add a note in the release notes.

alex: will do — creating revert PR now and kicking a CI run. thanks everyone. :tada:
